cures.text: Then cover the test block with a film and place it in a constant temperature and humidity curing chamber for curing (at 21 °C with a relative humidity of 98%). After 24 h, remove the mold and then place the sample back into the curing chamber to continue the curing process under the same conditions.

tests.propertyNote: Shrinkage strain from length change after demolding (JGJT70-2009), specimens kept in the 21 °C / 98% RH chamber; not a standard drying-shrinkage exposure
tests.specimen: 40 mm × 40 mm × 160 mm prisms, three per group

results.text: It can be found that when RG/L = 3, the 90 d shrinkage strain of the specimen is the highest (4928 με), which is 25.8% higher than that when RG/L = 1.5 (3917 με).
It can be found that when RG/L = 3, the 90 d shrinkage strain of the specimen is the highest (4928 με), which is 25.8% higher than that when RG/L = 1.5 (3917 με).
When RB/S = 0.21, the shrinkage strain is 3340 με. When RB/S = 0.39, the shrinkage strain increased by 39.8% to 4670 με.

gaps: Table quotes are mechanical joins of caption, header cells and row cells (format: 'Table N (caption): header → row').

Source inconsistencies kept visible: the text says ten groups but Table 2 lists twelve rows; RG/L-2.5, RB/S-0.33 and RW/B-0.37 have identical masses; the RB/S labels (0.21–0.39) equal sand/binder in Table 2 (e.g. 495/1500 = 0.33), not binder/sand; the RW/B labels equal Table 2 water/(GBFS+LS) (405/1500 = 0.27 … 855/1500 = 0.57), so they exclude the activator solution's water; the text says 'The ratios in Table 3 represent the materials required to make 3 samples' but means Table 2.
Batch basis: the text says the ratios 'in Table 3 represent the materials required to make 3 samples'; Table 3 is the model table, so reading Table 2 as a three-prism batch is inferred.
The activator mass per batch is not tabulated, so water accounting and total liquid are unresolved (the existing correction hold on this guide stays).
The text's water/binder comparison (36.7%) names no mix value and is contradictory (reduction and increase in the same paragraph); not transcribed.
Shrinkage was measured on specimens kept in the 98% RH chamber, so it is recorded as 'other' rather than drying shrinkage.
Every value awaits the second-reviewer check recorded in the batch audit before release.
